question.problem:
Let $⟨2,y⟩$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x+ky=5 \\ x+2y=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

I. $|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|$

II. $2|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|$

III. $|\begin{aligned}4 & k \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|=2|\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}|$

current_example.problem:
Let $\langle x,3 \rangle$ be the solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}5x-2y=4 \\ x+ky=8\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following equations could be solved to find the value of $k?$

I. ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14233012/assets/b765ae779efae1675d598cc9e9ff48b25db5171a43a418f5699e5587499c5950.svg)

II. ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14233012/assets/9abe37c4bd604a1a89197df74acb08c1a218756bfd7cf68e04fd0def6e7a22b8.svg)

III. ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14233012/assets/0d69348a40a2d173387c00f7335712c0e5763a34b7009682901e6e4829f191bc.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $y$ is given by $y=\dfrac{D_y}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{y} & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 1 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot 8-4\cdot 1 \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{{D}_{y}}{D} \\ 3 & =\frac{36}{|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}|} \\ |\begin{aligned}5 & -2 \\ 1 & k\end{aligned}| & =12\end{aligned}
$$

So, the correct answer is "II only".
